headline: US launches 9th night of strikes on Iran amid rising Middle East tensions
summary: The attacks target Iranian military capabilities in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil supply. This comes as Kuwait intercepts drones and Iran claims to have struck an "enemy command centre" in Syria.
details: New violence shook the Middle East early Monday as the United States announced another wave of attacks on Iran for the ninth consecutive night. Simultaneously, Kuwait reported intercepting hostile drones, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a "surprise attack" on an "enemy command centre" in Syria.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated that the strikes were aimed at "degrading Iranian military capabilities used to attack commercial vessels and civilian mariners" in the Strait of Hormuz. This strategic waterway is crucial for global oil supplies.

A preliminary deal to end the conflict has collapsed amidst a deadlock over the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil supplies transited before the war. Since February 28, Iran has targeted US allies and military assets, and has virtually blocked the strait.

Kuwaiti air defences engaged hostile drone attacks, with the army confirming that explosions heard were due to air defense systems intercepting these attacks. Bahrain's interior ministry also issued air raid sirens, urging residents to seek safety.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced a "surprise attack" on an enemy special operations command centre in Syria's Al-Tanf region. This was stated as revenge for "martyred soldiers of Iranshahr," according to state news agency IRNA.

Iran also claimed on Sunday to have targeted two US bases in Kuwait in response to intensifying attacks. Tehran asserts these attacks have hit transport and infrastructure sites, including an under-construction nuclear power plant.

The fresh rounds of violence followed a weekend where the US reported three new military fatalities and one service member missing in action. Two were killed in Iranian missile and drone attacks on Jordan, while another died in Iraq during the controlled detonation of an unexploded ordnance.

These deaths bring the confirmed number of American military fatalities to 17 since the war began on February 28. In contrast, Iran's health ministry reported 50 people killed and over 500 injured in recent fighting.

The UN's nuclear watchdog is investigating Iran's claim that the Darkhovin nuclear power plant was attacked, noting it contained no nuclear material during its last visit. The IAEA director reiterated calls for military restraint near all nuclear-related sites.

Hopes for a political settlement have dimmed, despite mediators' efforts to bring both sides back to the negotiating table. Iran's central military commander, Ali Abdollahi, warned that further US aggression would face a "decisive and devastating response."

headline_marked: [[Dhaka experiences moderate air quality]] on Monday morning
headline: Dhaka experiences moderate air quality on Monday morning
summary: Dhaka's air quality index (AQI) was reported as moderate, indicating acceptable air quality with some pollutants. This offers a temporary respite from often poor air conditions in the capital.
details: Dhaka's air quality was categorized as moderate on Monday morning. This indicates that the air pollution levels are acceptable, though some pollutants might pose a moderate health concern for a very small number of people.
Globally, Kampala, the capital of Uganda, was reported to have the worst air quality during the same period. This highlights the varying air pollution challenges faced by cities worldwide.
